planet.name: Mars
planet.lore: An alternate-future exploration anthology, not historical missions. ATLAS and TAIGA use conventional rover engineering; VANGUARD uses deliberately fictional pulse lift. Discoveries remain story proposals until approved as canon.
planet.visual_description: Barren Martian terrain: fine rusty ochre dust, dark basalt fragments, weathered layered outcrops, dry gravel and a distant eroded horizon under a muted dusty peach sky. No plants, cities, open water or people. Believable terrain scale and distant atmospheric haze.

photo_style: Photograph of a tangible full-size robotic vehicle, not a miniature. Restrained saturation, natural tonal transitions, fine material texture. Matte painted panels, subdued brushed-metal reflections, small dark sensor lenses. A few recessed fasteners, narrow panel seams and protected pivots at plausible scale. Every instrument is securely mounted; each arm has one continuous chain of connected joints. Suspension and propulsion have clearance to move. Sealed opaque equipment housings, no cabin or passenger windows. Preserve silhouette, equipment placement and propulsion type. No glossy toy finish, theatrical bloom, captions or graphic overlays.
reference_style: Engineering reference photograph on a seamless neutral WHITE floor and WHITE background. Soft broad light from above-left, gentle fill, faint contact shadow. Expose white body panels slightly darker than the backdrop so edges remain visible. Entire vehicle with clear margin, sharp focus across the body, moderate perspective like a 70mm lens. Clean baseline manufactured surfaces with subtle machining marks. No scenery, rocks, red dust, display pedestal or green reflections.
scene_style: Documentary photograph taken by a nearby robotic survey camera, ordinary 40mm-equivalent field of view at vehicle-body height. Available sunlight and sky fill, plausible directional shadows, restrained exposure, no studio lighting or theatrical rim light. Granular soil, irregular stones and fine dust in panel recesses, without excessive sharpening. Terrain occupies part of the frame to establish scale. Replace the white reference background entirely with the outdoor environment and relight the vehicle to match, not a pasted studio cutout.
reference_camera: Front-left three-quarter view at body height. Entire vehicle visible, front sampling tool on the near side, rear extending away. Arm folded into its travel cradle, propulsion hardware readable. Canonical baseline design.

vehicles.name: ATLAS-01

mission.name: First Light Survey
mission.purpose: Map a landing plain and inspect basalt exposures for later sampling routes.
mission.arrival: A robotic lander lowers a short ramp onto a broad stony plain.

vehicles.identity: ATLAS-01: roughly two-metre-long unmanned American aerospace-inspired Mars rover. Low rectangular warm-white equipment body, navy-blue inset side panels, flat charcoal deck. Six broad open-metal-mesh wheels, three per side, connect visibly to the chassis through dark articulated suspension and clear hubs. One short central mast carries a compact horizontal pair of camera lenses. One short two-joint sampling arm mounts at the FRONT centre of the chassis, ending in a small cylindrical contact tool; it folds against the front for travel. The rear is a plain sealed service panel. Matte ceramic-painted panels, brushed metal arm sections, dark protected pivots, a few recessed bolts. No loose cables, decorative fins or passenger compartment. Keep wheel, axle and suspension orientations mechanically coherent.
scenes: First morning after landing. Front-left view of the entire ATLAS on a broad rust-coloured plain. A small landing platform and short ramp sit in the middle distance behind it, connected by two bands of fresh wheel tracks. Low sunlight from frame left catches mesh wheel edges and casts a long grounded shadow to the right. Freshly deployed body with only a scattering of grit on lower panels and wheel contact patches. Camera upright, sampling arm folded. Fine foreground pebbles and a low dark ridge on the horizon. Quiet operational survey photograph, not a promotional hero shot.

ATLAS examines a dark fractured basalt boulder beside its front wheel. Front-right photograph, close enough to read contact while keeping the whole rover in frame. The single FRONT arm unfolds through two connected joints, cylindrical tool pressed against one rough rock face. Wheels support the rover firmly, far wheels naturally occluded. A small fresh pale abrasion marks the contact, a few fallen grains immediately beneath it. Side sunlight reveals rock pits, mesh wheel texture and fine dust around suspension pivots. No extra arm, floating instrument or dramatic debris cloud.

The same ATLAS after three Earth years, paused beside a shallow eroded valley. Left-side view with front angled slightly toward camera, rover about half the frame width. Original white and navy panels remain recognizable under uneven ochre dust: thicker in seams and sheltered corners, thinner on exposed edges. Small lower-panel paint chips and rubbed wheel contact surfaces, no catastrophic damage. Arm folded, mast intact, all original equipment attached. A curved wheel trail crosses wind-rippled sediment behind it. Hazy late-afternoon light, layered valley wall in the distance. Worn but maintained, not abandoned.

vehicles.name: TAIGA-02

mission.name: Deep Strata Expedition
mission.purpose: Inspect exposed sedimentary layers and collect shallow drill samples.
mission.arrival: A squat descent platform delivers the rover near an eroded basin rim.

vehicles.identity: TAIGA-02: roughly two-metre-long unmanned Russian planetary-exploration-inspired Mars rover. Squat cylindrical brushed-silver instrument housing with a closed flat top on a rectangular dark olive-green chassis. Four broad solid-metal wheels, two per side, with raised chevron ribs and dark hubs. Each wheel connects visibly to a sturdy short suspension arm. A short camera post sits at the FRONT edge of the circular housing with one dark lens block. One robust two-joint drilling arm mounts at the FRONT centre of the chassis, ending in a short cylindrical drill head, folded against the front for travel. Rear is a plain olive service panel. Restrained housing seams, recessed fasteners, matte green paint and enclosed dark joints. Scientific field instrument, no weaponry, cabin or ornamental antennas.
scenes: First survey after touchdown near an eroded basin. TAIGA fully visible from front-right on flat gravel beside shallow wind-shaped ridges. Its squat descent platform is small in the distance, a short pair of ribbed-wheel tracks leading toward the rover. Early sunlight reflects softly across the circular silver housing; green chassis and four ribbed wheels remain readable in open shadow. A little landing dust rests on the lower chassis, otherwise new surfaces. Drill folded, camera upright. Layered outcrops beyond the plain, no fog or excessive exhaust haze.

TAIGA inspects a low sedimentary outcrop at the foot of a dry basin slope. Front-left photograph showing the full rover and a metre-scale exposed ledge. The single drilling arm extends from its front mount through two solid joints, short drill head touching a pale horizontal rock band. A compact mound of fresh powder lies below the shallow drill point. Four wheels rest on stable gravel with plausible axle alignment. Fine dust on the silver housing, subdued metal reflections. Side light reveals thin irregular rock layers, fractures and raised wheel ribs. No sparks, giant drill rig, loose cables or extra tools.

TAIGA after three Earth years, still operating on a broad dry valley floor. Rear-right photograph preserves its circular silver housing and square green undercarriage, front drill folded on the far side. Red dust fills housing seams and wheel ribs. Olive paint is faded and locally scuffed on lower edges; silver surfaces dulled by abrasion, not mirror polished. Suspension and camera intact. A recent wheel trail curves between scattered stones. Low stratified escarpment recedes into a dusty horizon. Soft available afternoon light and ordinary expedition-camera framing, enduring scientific machine rather than cinematic wreck.

vehicles.name: VANGUARD-03

mission.name: Far Reach Demonstrator
mission.purpose: Reach crater terrain inaccessible to wheels using experimental pulse lift.
mission.arrival: A robotic carrier releases the probe near a small crater.
mission.fiction_boundary: Pulse lift is invented; visible supports, shadows and dust interaction must remain coherent.

vehicles.identity: VANGUARD-03: unmanned Marvel-inspired exploration probe about two metres across, tangible scientific machine rather than superhero costume. Low hexagonal deep-crimson body, flat graphite deck, satin-gold inset side panels. NO wheels. Three identical downward pulse-thruster housings form a balanced triangle firmly integrated beneath the body; fictional pulse lift enables low hover. Three short hinged landing legs attach around the lower rim with broad footpads clear of the outlets. One short central camera mast carries a dark lens block. One compact two-joint sampling arm attaches to a distinct FRONT panel, folded against it for travel; opposite rear panel plain. Matte red paint, dark heat-resistant nozzle rims, lightly brushed gold panels and tidy recessed fasteners. No cockpit, floating components, giant energy core or weapons.
vehicles.reference_pose: For reference photography, rest the probe on its three extended landing legs on the white floor. Thrusters OFF, no glow or dust plume. Arm folded. Keep all three thruster housings, allowing natural occlusion.
scenes: Immediately after arrival at a shallow crater, VANGUARD hovers half a metre above the ground in full front-left view. Landing legs folded clear of outlets, arm folded. Only restrained pale glow inside dark thruster rims, no long flames. Low irregular dust veil spreads close to the surface; a separate shadow falls below and slightly right of the probe. New crimson and satin-gold panels carry a few dust grains. Small carrier platform distant near crater rim. Early side sunlight, textured stony foreground, empty dusty sky. No wheel tracks or superhero effects.

VANGUARD has landed beside a fractured dark rock inside a shallow crater. Front-right photograph at body height showing the entire probe, rock and support contacts. Three landing legs extended, broad footpads firmly planted. Pulse thrusters completely OFF: dark outlets, no airborne dust. One front sampling arm reaches from its mount through two connected joints to touch a fresh fracture. Small pebbles around footpads, little pale powder at the contact. Graphite deck, crimson shell and gold panels have subdued natural reflections and fine settled dust. Clear late-morning light. No wheels, additional arms or floating instruments.

VANGUARD after three Earth years, hovering low across a weathered crater floor. Rear-right photograph with layered crater rim distant. Original hexagonal crimson body and gold panels recognizable but dulled by uneven dust and small abrasions. Thicker dust in protected seams, subtle wear on leading edges, local heat discoloration on dark nozzle rims without dramatic soot. Arm folded on far front panel; legs folded clear of three working thrusters. Restrained ground-hugging dust disturbance and separated shadow establish hover height. Muted sunlight through atmospheric dust, scattered rocks, no wheel tracks. Worn but maintained, not abandoned.
